regime_notes: Scores in this pillar are flow-based (+1 for inflows, -1 for outflows, 0 for mixed) from the October monthly reports and the Oct 26-30 European weekly data. They are not fundamental views. US-listed ETFs took $211bn in October (State Street; $204bn per TD/Bloomberg), the second-largest month ever, with a record $74bn into bonds and 80% of equity flows going to US exposures as non-US equities sold off. Sector flows went to tech and energy, while industrials, consumer, utilities and real estate bled. Gold is split by region: US outflows, but record global holdings driven by Europe and Asia, which is supportive for IGLN. No closure, merger, fee or index change was found for VWRA, SSAC/ACWD, IWDA, CSPX, VUAA, CNDX, EIMI, IGLN or AGGU in the window. The most recent fee event found for these funds is Vanguard's cut of the FTSE All-World UCITS ETF OCF from 0.19% to 0.14%, effective 2026-07-28. Gaps: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-run, so the 2026 scan of US universe tickers for closures, mergers, ticker changes and fee changes is incomplete. Utilities/real estate, clean energy, small/mid value, multi-asset/alt, Japan and China had only one flow source or ambiguous categories and are left unscored; see the digest.

red_flags.issue: Fee cut, a favourable change rather than a risk: Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF OCF cut from 0.19% to 0.14%, effective 2026-07-28 (announced 2026-07-21). The cut applies at fund level, so it covers the VWRA share class.

Scan incomplete: the shared web-search budget was exhausted before targeted 2026 closure, merger, ticker-change and fee-change searches for universe tickers could run. The searches that did run turned up no such event for any universe ticker; the liquidations they found (MEMY, the Tidal real-estate ETFs, the T-REX 2X funds AFRU/TEUP/ASUP/SBTU, Themes and Defiance funds) are all outside the universe. Re-run this check before relying on the absence of flags.

Not a fund-level event, recorded for context: SPY had the largest passive equity outflow in October (-$6.9bn) while VOO (+$23.7bn) and SPYM (+$10.1bn) led inflows, a continuing fee-driven rotation. No change to the fund.

Not a fund-level event, recorded for context: GLD lost $1.8bn in October while GLDM gained $905m, so US gold ETF flows were net -$0.7bn against global gold ETF inflows of +$2.7bn. No change to the fund.

upcoming_events.event: Expected effective date of the MSCI November 2026 semi-annual index review, by MSCI's usual end-November timetable; the announcement usually comes in mid-November. Neither date is verified for 2026. The review affects IWDA, SSAC/ACWD and EIMI.
Approximate release of November US ETF flow reports (State Street flash flows) and the WGC November gold ETF flows, used to re-check this pillar's flow scores.
